title: A Simple Counting Argument for Dense Linear Hypergraphs
summary: In connection to the Brown-Erdős-Sós conjecture, we give a short local averaging proof of a density theorem for linear uniform hypergraphs. Let $r \ge 3$, $k \ge 3$, and suppose that $n \ge (r-2)(k-2)+1$. If $H$ is a linear $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices and \[|E(H)| \geq \frac{k-2}{r^2((r-2)(k-2)+1)}n^2 + \frac{n}{r},\] then $H$ contains $k$ edges spanning at most $(r-2)k+3$ vertices. In the standard linear-density normalization, this gives the asymptotic density threshold $c \geq \frac{r-1}{r} \cdot \frac{k-2}{(r-2)(k-2)+1} + o(1)$.
